North Providence planning board continues Beard Avenue project to Nov. 10
The applicant's attorney said the environmental engineer handling the case had been sick for six weeks, delaying a report needed before the hearing could proceed.
The North Providence Planning Board voted to continue a public hearing on a 48-unit residential adaptive reuse project at 114 Beard Avenue to Nov. 10, after the applicant's attorney requested more time to address environmental issues raised at a prior meeting.
The board met Wednesday, Oct. 14, at the North Providence council chambers, 2000 Smith Street.
THE DELAY Attorney Jack McGreen, representing applicant Patriot Builders, asked for the continuance so the project's environmental engineer could respond to issues raised at the September meeting. "We had a little bit of difficult time reaching our environmental engineer," McGreen said. "Apparently he was sick for like the last six weeks and we just recently engaged him on Friday."
McGreen confirmed his client agreed to waive the 90-day decision deadline so the board could continue the matter past its usual time limit. The board chairman also asked the applicant to waive an additional period to allow a decision before Jan. 1, which McGreen accepted, extending the effective deadline to Dec. 9.
SCHEDULING The board discussed several possible continuance dates, complicated by the Nov. 11 regular meeting falling on Veterans Day, when town hall is closed. After ruling out other dates due to room and attorney availability, board member Lou Dukio moved to continue the matter to a date certain of Nov. 10, seconded by Steve Patassi. The motion passed on a voice vote.
The board chairman confirmed the item would be heard at "our newly scheduled planning board meeting November Tuesday, November 10th at 6 p.m."
